title: Nearby contacts gave no clear phase link among 21 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested whether distinct inputs with nearby contacts onto motor neuron DE-3R had similar coherence phases in one leech ganglion. We used linked electron microscopy and voltage imaging. The primary cohort had 21 inputs, 191 sites, and 210 distinct input pairs. At a 10 micrometre path radius, the mean correlation across two swim trials was 0.01348. A whole-input label test with 19,999 draws gave p = 0.44245. None of 24 path-radius and trial tests passed a joint correction. Including 35 mapped inputs gave mean r = 0.03092 and p = 0.23870. The test gives no clear positive evidence for this local phase rule. It does not establish absence of an effect. We provide code, derived tables, null draws, source hashes, figures, and independent checks. One animal, selected inputs, uncertain tracing, and missing raw phase errors limit inference. The results do not establish a rule across animals or behaviors.
